extracted.intended_audience: math content creators and judges participating in the Summer of Math Exposition (SoME)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or producing entries for the Summer of Math Exposition (SoME): online math exposition pieces (videos, articles, interactive posts) judged by peer review and voting. The page describes the event phases and highlights qualities of top entries (originality, intuition, interactivity, audience alignment, constructive feedback).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive feedback in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: You’ll be shown a series of entries to review, vote on, and give constructive feedback. It’s a chance to reflect, learn, and help others improve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be constructive and aimed at helping authors improve; the peer-review phase is explicitly positioned as an opportunity to reflect, learn, and help others improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review and voting (community evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase 2: Peer Review and Voting — You’ll be shown a series of entries to review, vote on, and give constructive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are evaluated by the community via peer review and voting; both qualitative feedback and quantitative votes factor into rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of math content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summer of Math Exposition (SoME) is an annual competition fostering the creation of excellent math content online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should aim to be high-quality mathematical expositions — accurate, thoughtful, and well-presented — suitable for publication as online math content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes examples like 'an original, nonstandard visualization of the Hopf fibration' and entries that 'share something students cannot easily find in the textbook.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel perspectives, uncommon techniques, or original visualizations that present material in a way not commonly found in standard texts are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries aim to 'make them genuinely intuitive' and 'presents some geometric intuition for π₁/π₂/π₃' or 'build up to the actual definitions of P and NP through a series of examples.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should prioritize making concepts intuitive, using explanations and examples that build understanding rather than only formal statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness / pedagogical utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples emphasize sharing techniques 'students cannot easily find in the textbook' and methods 'easy to remember and use for a lot of math problems,' with the author noting 'it helped me a lot when solving a polynomial equation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that provide practical problem-solving techniques, memorable heuristics, or pedagogical value for students and teachers are highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target-audience appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: 'This post is written for undergraduates who have some probability background. You'll get the most out of this if you're familiar with basic Markov chain concepts (states, transition matrices, etc).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should clearly target an appropriate audience and set or assume suitable prerequisites; alignment with the stated audience (e.g., undergraduates) is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visualizations and interactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Several highlighted entries emphasize visual/interactive elements: 'animated explainer', 'interactive visualizations that let you explore the ideas hands-on', and visual intuition for abstract concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective visual or interactive components that enhance intuition and allow hands-on exploration are explicitly praised and considered a strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth, insight, and broader perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are commended for offering insight into how theory is made and for explaining 'why such natural patterns emerge' or giving 'a glimpse into the patient, creative craft of theoretical science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond presenting facts, submissions that provide deeper insight, historical/contextual framing, or perspectives on how scientists think and build models are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative and exposition quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlighted pieces 'take the reader on a journey' and 'begin with familiar scenes' to introduce topics, indicating attention to storytelling and exposition structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good narrative structure, engaging openings, and a guided progression that helps readers/viewers follow the development of ideas contribute to a strong submission.
